name: tako-mcp
title: Tako MCP Server
description: Tako MCP gives your agent premium live data from authoritative providers and web search in one call, returned as cited charts and web results. The data covers finance, markets, company KPIs, economics, website traffic, sports, prediction markets, demographics, energy, real estate, and more.

authentication.description: Web hosts (Claude.ai, ChatGPT) connect via the server's OAuth flow. CLI/desktop hosts pass a Tako API token (from tako.com account settings) as a Bearer credential.

tools.name: tako_agent
tools.description:
Run Tako's Answer Agent. It plans, queries the data graph and the web over several steps, and returns a written `answer` with numbered citations plus the chart `cards` it built. Start a run only when the user asks for one: they name Tako's agent or ask for deep or multi-step research with Tako. Otherwise, use `tako_search`.

Best for: an ask for Tako's agent whose answer is a chart or a written finding, not a list of companies or people.

A call returns within 45 s. If `status` is `running`, call again with `run_id`; don't start a new run. In your reply, link each card's `url`; the full list or chart lives on that page.

query.description: The question to research, in natural language. Ask one question per call; the agent plans its own sub-steps. Send `query` or `run_id`, not both.

run_id.description: A `run_id` from an earlier call that returned `status: running`. Send it instead of `query` to keep waiting for that run.

sources.description: Which corpora to search; default is both. `data` is Tako's data graph, curated from authoritative data sources; `web` is the open web. Keep both unless the user asks for one. A thread keeps its sources, so omit this on a follow-up.

thread_id.description: A `thread_id` from an earlier run. Pass it back to ask a follow-up in that conversation; omit it to start a new one.

tools.name: tako_available_data
tools.description:
Find what data Tako holds on an entity or a metric, and the canonical name it holds it under.

Best for: questions about what Tako covers. Put a company, person, or place in `q` to list the metrics tracked on it; put a metric in `q` to list the entities it covers. Add `metric` when you know the measure — you get the resolved pair and a ready-to-run `next_call`.

Search on the canonical names it returns, not your own phrasing — `tako_search` matches the graph's names, not yours. A name here means the graph tracks it, not that a card exists. If the follow-up search comes back empty, say Tako has no card for it rather than rephrasing the query. Hand a node id to `tako_graph_related` to see what else connects to it.

q.description: The entity or metric to look up by name — "Carnival", "United States", "Nvidia". Put the measure in `metric`, not here.

metric.description: The measure, when you already know it — "gross margin", "capex". Supplying it resolves the entity+metric pair directly; omit it to browse everything the entity has.

types.description: Narrow resolution to one kind, an entity or a metric. Omit to resolve both.

label.description: NER label to prefer for `q` — a boost, not a filter. Set it when you can categorize the term: company → ORG, place → GPE, person → PERSON. It never applies to `metric`.

limit.description: How many candidates to resolve for each of `q` and `metric`. Raising it widens what the tool considers, not just what it shows: a deeper metric can become the one `next_call` names.

tools.name: tako_company_agent
tools.description:
Run Tako's Company Agent. It searches company registries, business profiles, and the web over several steps, and returns a written `answer` with numbered citations plus the list `cards` it built. Start a run only when the user asks for one: they name Tako's agent or ask for deep or multi-step research with Tako. Otherwise, use `tako_search`, even for a list that search can't fully filter.

Best for: an ask for Tako's Company Agent, or an ask for Tako's agent to build a list of companies or of their professionals, for prospecting or hiring. It filters companies by location, industry, status, founding date, funding stage, or size, and their executives by role, seniority, or department, and finds the officers, directors, and controllers in company registries.

A call returns within 45 s. If `status` is `running`, call again with `run_id`; don't start a new run. In your reply, link each card's `url`; the full list or chart lives on that page.

query.description: The question to research, in natural language. Ask one question per call; the agent plans its own sub-steps. Send `query` or `run_id`, not both.

run_id.description: A `run_id` from an earlier call that returned `status: running`. Send it instead of `query` to keep waiting for that run.

sources.description: Which sources to research. `data` is Tako's data graph, curated from authoritative data sources; `web` is the open web. A new thread uses both. Keep both unless the user asks for one. A thread keeps its sources, so omit this on a follow-up.

thread_id.description: A `thread_id` from an earlier run. Pass it back to ask a follow-up in that conversation; omit it to start a new one.

effort.description: Research depth. `medium` is the default. `high` is stronger and slower. `low` answers from the company registry and the web only, and can't filter or rank by financial metrics such as revenue or headcount. Effort is fixed for a thread.

tools.name: tako_company_enrich
tools.description:
Match up to 25 known companies by website, LinkedIn page or name. Returns per-item `results` and one list card of matches.

Use to look up companies you can name, such as a list of domains.

`results` has one entry per item, in order: status (matched, no_match, failed), match_id, confidence (exact, high, ambiguous), matched_on, alternates, unresolved, failed. Card `description` previews 10 rows: name, status, estimated_revenue*, headcount, industry, funding_stage, total_raised, last_funding_date, investors, location, website, tako_url. `tako_contents` on its `url` returns every row: those fields except last_funding_date and investors, plus company_type, linkedin_followers*, linkedin_url, ticker, established, parent*, subsidiaries*, description, headcount_range, tags, metro, naics_codes, postcode, funding_round_count, funding_rounds, sic_codes, also_known_as, other_domains, street_address, twitter_url, facebook_url, sources. * is premium: null unless that call sets `premium: true`.

items.description: The companies to match, 1 to 25. Each needs `domain`, `linkedin_url` or `name`. `domain` and `linkedin_url` match exactly, and `name` by score. `city`, `region`, `country` and `industry` rank a name's matches and never exclude one.

tools.name: tako_company_search
tools.description:
Screen active companies by industry, place, size, founding year, funding stage and ownership. Returns `total`, the filters `applied`, `notes` and one list card.

Use to build a list of companies from filters, such as Series B enterprise SaaS companies in the US.

Card `description` previews 10 rows: name, status, estimated_revenue*, headcount, industry, funding_stage, total_raised, last_funding_date, investors, location, website, tako_url. `tako_contents` on its `url` returns every row: those fields except last_funding_date and investors, plus company_type, linkedin_followers*, linkedin_url, ticker, established, parent*, subsidiaries*, description, headcount_range, tags, metro, naics_codes, postcode, funding_round_count, funding_rounds, sic_codes, also_known_as, other_domains, street_address, twitter_url, facebook_url, sources. * is premium: null unless that call sets `premium: true`. `total` stops at 500, and `total_is_lower_bound` says when. It can't filter or sort by revenue.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or English name.

region.description: State or province, as a name or an ISO 3166-2 code.

town.description: Town of the headquarters, or of the registered office when there's no headquarters. Needs country or region beside it.

industry.description: An industry name, alias or id, such as fintech or aerospace and defense. `applied` shows what it was read as.

startups.description: Startups: private companies founded in the last ten years (unless founded_after or founded_before names other years), of a startup type (not a government body, nonprofit, school or public company's subsidiary), that raised a venture round or have at most 500 employees.

founded_after.description: Founded in this year or later.

founded_before.description: Founded in this year or earlier.

order_by.description: A field to sort by. A leading minus sorts it in descending order.

tools.name: tako_contents
tools.description:
Fetch the full content behind a url: a web page's text, or an exportable Tako card's data rows. Batch up to 10 urls in one call — each fails on its own.

Fetch only cards that `tako_search` marked `exportable: true`. Set `max_rows` when the recent rows are enough. If a page is long, such as a filing or an annual report, set `query` to a question to get back only the passages that answer it.

Best for: reading one source in full — a page you need to quote, or the rows behind a card you need to compute over.

urls.description: The urls to fetch: a Tako card url or a web result url. One call for 8 urls saves 7 round trips.

max_rows.description: Tako cards only: how many rows to return. Omit it to get up to 2,000 rows. With `delivery: "link"`, you can raise it to 100,000. Charges scale with rows returned, so lower it when the recent rows are enough.

max_chars.description: Web pages only: character cap on the extracted text. Inline fetches default to 100,000 per url, less across a batch. Raise it for a long document; `truncated` reports a cut. With `query`, it caps the passages instead: 100 to 20,000, and 4,000 by default.

query.description: Web pages only: a question the passages should answer. The result holds those passages instead of the page. Omit it to get the whole page.

delivery.description: Tako cards only. `inline` returns the data in the result. `link` returns a download link: a CSV file, or a JSON file with `format: "card"`. It expires in 5 minutes. Use `link` when you can run shell commands and want to analyze the data in code. If the download fails, call again inline with `max_rows` at 2,000 or less.

format.description: Tako cards only. `rows` returns the card's data as one table. `card` returns the card's own structure, such as a company card's tabs or a game's box score.

offset.description: Tako list cards only: rows to skip. With `max_rows: 1`, it fetches a single row.

premium.description: Tako cards only: `true` returns premium cells, shown as 🔒. Charges scale with the rows that hold one, so set it only when the user asks. For one row, pass its own Tako link with `max_rows: 1`. Otherwise set `offset` and `max_rows`.

tools.name: tako_graph_related
tools.description:
Explore what a graph node connects to — its metrics, the entities a metric covers, competitors, industry, index membership, and sources.

Two modes. Pass `node_id` alone for the map: every relation group with its key, label, total, and its first 3 names. Pass `relation` to page one group, where each item comes back with the id that explores it. Read a key off the map rather than guessing — an unknown key returns an empty group, not an error.

Best for: expanding a node you already resolved. Resolve a name to a node id with `tako_available_data` first. A metric listed here means the graph tracks it, not that a card exists — `tako_search` is the final check.

node_id.description: Public id of the node to explore, as returned by `tako_available_data` or on a `tako_search` card.

relation.description: Relation key to page, taken from the map: metrics, entities, siblings, part_of, members, or a named edge like rel:competes_with. Omit for the map.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on names and aliases, one string per call: "revenue" matches `Total Revenue` and misses `Sales`. Call once per name variant.

label.description: NER label to prefer among the related nodes — a boost, not a filter.

infer_label.description: Detect labels from `q`. Omit it and the server infers them whenever `q` is set.

cursor.description: Page handle from a previous drilled relation. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Page size for a drilled relation. Omit it and the server serves 50. Ignored on the map, where every group returns its first 3 names whatever you pass.

tools.name: tako_people_search
tools.description:
Screen employees by role, place and employer. Returns `total`, the filters `applied`, `notes`, `unresolved`, `failed` and one list card.

Use to build a list of people from filters, such as heads of sales at Series B startups in Texas.

Card `description` previews 10 rows: name, title, department, employer, schools, in_role_since, location, linkedin_url, work_email*, phone*, personal_email*, tako_url. `tako_contents` on its `url` returns every row: those fields except schools, plus seniority, description, education, experience, registry_seats, sub_role, business_area, occupation, job_summary, skills, industry, metro, job_verified_on, twitter_url, github_url, all_emails*, all_personal_emails*, employer_{industry, tako_industries, tags, size, funding_stage, founded, location, listing}, sources. * is premium: null unless that call sets `premium: true`. `total` stops at 500, and `total_is_lower_bound` says when.

role.description: Title, seniority or function phrases, such as 'head of sales'.

company_ids.description: Employer ids, such as the `match_id` of a matched company.

person_country.description: Where the person is: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or English name.

person_region.description: Where the person is: state or province.

person_metro.description: Where the person is: metropolitan area.

person_town.description: Needs person_country or person_region beside it.

company_industry.description: The employer's industry: a name, alias or id, such as fintech. `applied` shows what it was read as.

company_startups.description: Employers that are startups: private companies founded in the last ten years, of a startup type, that raised a venture round or have at most 500 employees.

linkedin_urls.description: LinkedIn profile URLs. It narrows a search, so set another filter beside it.

emails.description: Email addresses. It narrows a search, so set another filter beside it.

phones.description: Phone numbers. It narrows a search, so set another filter beside it.

tools.name: tako_person_enrich
tools.description:
Match up to 25 known people by email, phone, LinkedIn profile or name. Returns per-item `results` and one list card of matches.

Use to look up known people, such as a contact list.

`results` has one entry per item, in order: status (matched, no_match, failed), match_id, confidence (exact, high, ambiguous), matched_on, alternates, unresolved, failed. Card `description` previews 10 rows: name, title, department, employer, schools, in_role_since, location, linkedin_url, work_email*, phone*, personal_email*, tako_url. `tako_contents` on its `url` returns every row: those fields except schools, plus seniority, description, education, experience, registry_seats, sub_role, business_area, occupation, job_summary, skills, industry, metro, job_verified_on, twitter_url, github_url, all_emails*, all_personal_emails*, employer_{industry, tako_industries, tags, size, funding_stage, founded, location, listing}, sources. * is premium: null unless that call sets `premium: true`.

items.description: The people to match, 1 to 25. Each needs `email`, `phone`, `linkedin_url` or `name`. The first three match exactly, and `name` by score. `company_domain`, `company_name` and `title` are hints for a name. Give a phone with its country code.

tools.name: tako_search
tools.description:
Search Tako's data graph and the web in one call: many results at once, as structured cards plus web results. The first card's chart renders inline; some hosts also show every other card's chart, in search's order.

It finds results; `tako_contents` fetches what's behind them. Each card carries a headline value, node ids, and a url — pass the url to `tako_contents` for rows (`exportable: true` cards) or a web result's full page text. When `exportable` is false the rows are locked — read the headline value from the card's `description`.

Best for: breadth — fan out several narrow queries in parallel. Each query answers one question — one metric for one entity, a comparison set ("Apple revenue", "Nvidia vs AMD gross margin"), one news or web lookup ("EU AI Act timeline"), or one list of companies, or of business professionals by role and place, for prospecting or recruiting ("fintechs in London", "CFOs in Austin"); several metrics or topics in one query retrieve poorly.

query.description: Natural-language search query (e.g. "US GDP growth", "Intel vs Nvidia revenue"). Double-quote a multi-word name to keep it one entity ("tesla motors" club revenue); an unpaired quote disables quoting. Website-traffic data is keyed by domain — query "openai.com monthly visits", not "OpenAI website visits".

sources.description: Which corpora to search; default is both. `data` is Tako's data graph, curated from authoritative data sources; `web` is the open web. Keep both unless the user asks for one.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for localized results. Omit it and the server uses US. Set it to localize for the user.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale tag for language and formatting. Omit it and the server uses en-US. Set it to localize for the user.

tools.name: tako_search_advanced
tools.description:
Get one citation-backed answer (`include_answer: true`), or search Tako's data graph and the web with the whole v3 request: per-source counts, inline card rows, graph pins, web domain and category filters, and the deep effort tier.

Only `query` is required; an omitted field takes the server default its description names. Naming a source block (even `{}`) selects it; omit both to search data and web. `data.include_contents` inlines each card's rows, billed per card — cap with `data.max_rows`, or fetch a card's rows with `tako_contents` instead.

Best for: a written answer (`include_answer` puts it in `answer`), or a call `tako_search` can't express. `output_schema` fills a JSON Schema from the evidence into `structured_output`.

query.description: Natural-language search query. One metric per query retrieves best. Double-quote a multi-word name to keep it one entity.

effort.description: Search effort. Omit it and the server uses fast. instant serves cached embeds; deep widens retrieval and reranks, at a premium rate.

location.description: End-user coordinates, for queries whose location is implicit (weather). A location named in the query wins; web results follow country_code.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for localization. Omit it and the server uses US.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale tag for language and formatting. Omit it and the server uses en-US.

timezone.description: IANA timezone. It formats dates in rendered card images only.

output_settings.description: Settings that control the response shape.

include_related.description: Maximum follow-up queries to return in `related`. Ignored when `include_answer` is true.

data.description: Tako data (card) source settings; naming it selects the data graph.

web.description: Web source settings; naming it selects the web.

include_answer.description: Set true to synthesize one citation-backed answer from the retrieval into `answer`.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema for the answer to fill, returned in `structured_output`. Needs `include_answer: true`; instant effort 400s. Type a field ["number", "null"] when evidence may be missing — Tako then signals that, not a zero.

tools.name: tako_visualize
tools.description:
Create a public, permanent Tako card from data you already have — to chart data Tako already holds, use `tako_search`. Tako stores what you send, the card never expires, and anyone with the returned url can open it without signing in. Confirm the user wants a public card before you call, then give them the url.

Never put sensitive data in `components`: no passwords, API keys, payment-card or bank details, health information, government identifiers, precise home addresses, or personal data the subject hasn't agreed to publish. Aggregate or anonymize it first, or decline.

Each component is `{component_type, config}`, rendered top to bottom. A titled bar chart is two: {"components": [{"component_type": "header", "config": {"title": "Revenue"}}, {"component_type": "categorical_bar", "config": {"datasets": [{"label": "Sales", "units": "USD", "data": [{"x": "NA", "y": 500}]}]}}]}. Use `person_card` alone, never beside another component.

components.description: The card's content blocks, rendered top to bottom.

title.description: The card's title. Omit it and a `header` component's title is used.

description.description: Card description, shown under the title.

source.description: Data source attribution, shown in the card footer.

height.description: Card height in pixels. Omit it and the card uses its default aspect-ratio height.

normalize_currencies.description: Convert currency-denominated datasets to this ISO 4217 code (e.g. `USD`) using historical rates.
